subject: Clarify billing units for long-context chat + bundle pricing
messages:
From: Sophie Rey <sophie@brightfin.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: BrightFin Procurement <procurements@brightfin.com>
Date: 2026-07-18T13:12:00-04:00
Subject: Billing unit details for our high-context flows + bundle ask

Hi Jordan,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — BrightFin is excited about the low-latency routing and the cache ideas. Before procurement and engineering get too deep, procurement has a few specific questions about how units are measured so we can model costs for an annual committed plan:

1) Context accounting: our product frequently sends a 40–60k token context (long document + conversation history) once at session start and then issues many short follow-ups (1–20 tokens). Do you bill the full context tokens on every subsequent follow-up if the client session references the same context via a sticky session or KV cache? Or only for the initial request that primes the session?

2) Streaming & partial tokens: when you stream tokens back to the client, is billing calculated against the final assembled token count, or is there an intermediate rounding behavior per-chunk? Example: if a streaming chunk produces 0.7 of a token (sub-token bytes) that completes into a full token across chunks, how is that billed?

3) Small-embedding rounding: we batch embeddings (100 items per batch). Some items are very short (<3 chars). Are you billing per-item rounding up to one full token, or are you billing based on total bytes/tokens of the batch?

4) Minimums / per-request floors: is there a minimum billed unit per API call or session (e.g., always at least 1 token or a per-request minimum dollar charge) that would affect high-volume, low-token-rate workflows?

5) Bundling / committed discounts: procurement is interested in a committed monthly token spend model with tiers and a true-up at month end. Do you support applying committed discounts to both hosted and dedicated options? If so, what are the mechanics (monthly invoice credit vs adjusted per-token rate)?

If you can point to a short write-up we can share internally (or a one-pager for procurement), that would be ideal. We can also set a quick call with procurement (they're EST) if easier.

Thanks,
— Sophie
Sophie Rey
Head of Platform Integrations | BrightFin
Sophie@brightfin.com

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Re: Billing unit details for our high-context flows + bundle ask

Hi Sophie — great questions, and thanks for the clear examples. I wanted to capture the answers here so procurement has something they can model from; I'll attach a short pricing summary too. TL;DR: billing is input_tokens + output_tokens per request (with a couple of important notes on caching, batching, and discounts). Details below.

1) Context accounting (sticky sessions / KV cache):
- For hosted API: we bill the tokens that are actually sent in the HTTP request. If you send the full 50k token context every time, you will be charged for it each request.
- If you use our session/KV-prefix caching (or a pinned context on Dedicated), the server may avoid re-sending the full context over the wire. Billing only counts tokens transmitted in the request: so if you prime the session once and subsequent requests reference a cached prefix that isn't re-sent, those later requests are billed only for the new tokens (the prompt you include plus completions).
- Important caveat: some SDK integrations will still serialize and send the context; you should use our session token binding APIs or the Dedicated sticky-context feature to avoid re-sending.

2) Streaming and token rounding:
- We only bill completed tokens. Streaming sends bytes/chunks to the client but our meter counts the finalized tokenization the model used for billing. There is no per-chunk rounding that leads to double billing; the final tokenized output is what matters.

3) Embeddings and batching:
- Embeddings are billed against the tokenized input for each item. If you batch 100 items into one request, we sum token counts across items in the batch and bill that total — we do not automatically round per-item to 1 token. So very short items benefit from batching.

4) Minimums / per-request floors:
- There is no additional per-request dollar floor for hosted pay-as-you-go customers beyond the token math (we bill whole tokens — effectively rounding up to the next token). The smallest unit is 1 token; very small requests that tokenize to 0.x will still bill as 1 token because tokens are integer units.
- For Dedicated / Reserved customers we use a different accounting model (reserved capacity + throughput units) and minimum monthly commitments apply per the contract.

5) Bundles / committed discounts:
- We can apply committed spend discounts to hosted plans with a 12-month commitment (monthly true-ups). Mechanically this is handled two ways depending on procurement preference:
  a) Adjusted per-token rate: we apply a reduced per-token rate for the committed volume bucket; usage above the bucket is billed at the overage rate.
  b) Monthly invoice credit: you pay a committed spend amount, and we apply that as credit each month; overage is billed normally.
- For Dedicated, discounts are applied at the contract/seat level (reserved GPU pools) rather than token-rate; however we can model a hybrid structure for BrightFin if you want committed spend applied against a Dedicated footprint.

Attachments: I attached a short one-pager (pricing_summary_Q3.pdf) that shows effective per-token math under a few commitment tiers, and a sample SOW we typically use (SOW_draft_v1.docx).

Next steps: if procurement wants a number we can provide a sample amortized monthly rate with three tiers (standard, committed-12mo, committed-24mo) and a proposed onboarding credit for the first month. Would you like me to put those numbers into a short quote (1 page) for procurement?

Happy to hop on a quick call — I'm EST as well.

Best,

Hi Sophie — looping in a couple quick procurement/ops notes from our side.

- We can offer a one-time onboarding credit equal to one month of estimated committed spend for first-time enterprise customers who sign 12-months. That helps during the initial test/parallel run.
- For the committed discounts, we prefer adjusted per-token rates (simpler for billing), but we can do invoice-credit if your finance team prefers a single committed payment.
- SOC2 + infosec artifacts: we have a SOC 2 Type II pack and an audit summary we can share behind an NDA. If your security team wants to run the questionnaire, we can set up a shared Drive link and a bridge call.

Jordan — can you share the three-tier quote by EOD EST? Sophie — if procurement can confirm target committed monthly spend (ballpark is fine) I’ll size the onboarding credit.

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor

Thanks — that all helps. A couple quick clarifications so procurement can finalize modeling:

• You said "we bill completed tokens" for streaming — to confirm: if a single response is emitted over N streaming chunks and the tokenizer only recognizes a token boundary at chunk N, we will be billed for that final token once. No incremental rounding per chunk. That matches what we need.
• Embeddings batching behaviour is perfect — we’ll batch short items to avoid per-item rounding.
• For session caching: procurement will require a short note we can add to the vendor evaluation stating that cached prefixes will not be billed again unless re-sent; can you provide a one-line we can paste?

If you can send the 3-tier quote and the short SOC2 artifact link (we'll sign an NDA), we can get this into our internal SSO approval flow next week. Once the numbers look good, we’ll route the SOW to legal for review — please include the DocuSign link when you’re ready.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — we should be able to move fast.

Best,
Sophie
